messages:
maya-eng: noticing a spike of 502s from eu-west after the rollout. metrics show ~18% of traffic still hitting green, error rate x10 vs baseline. can anyone confirm routing leaks?

deploy-bot: deploy 2026.3.4 started -> staged traffic shift to green (region-weight=20%) at 3701234500 :shipit:

pagerduty: INC12345 paging evan-sre — high error rate on eu-west gateway (service: inference-edge). escalate if no ack in 2m.

ev an-sre: acked, taking pager. joining now.

ev an-sre: logs look like 502s from edge->green-backend connection resets. green backend health checks show intermittent 500s, but control plane shows green healthy in eu-west cluster. suspect cache/DNS staleness at edge.

maya-eng: we flipped via region-weight, not DNS, but CF edge nodes might have cached old route entries. TTL was set low but some nodes have longer caching windows.

lisa-reliability: tagging runbook: "regional-rollout-failure" — recommending immediate kill-switch to route traffic off green and revert.

ops-runbook-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/regional-rollout-failure — steps: 1) set region-weight 100->blue, 2) disable canary flag, 3) monitor 5m, 4) open postmortem if error >5% for 10m.

thomas-customer-success: heads-up: two enterprise tenants in eu-west reported 5xxs via support channel. CX on it. need blast radius estimate.

ev an-sre: executing immediate mitigation — attempting feature-flag kill to stop new green traffic, and initiating region-weight rollback.

lisa-reliability: suggested commands:
```
# revert traffic at control plane
redwoodctl rollout set-weight --region eu-west --variant blue --weight 100
# force disable new variant via feature flag
redwoodctl flags set --name rollout-green --env eu-west --value off
```

maya-eng: FYI toggling flag will only affect control-plane-aware clients; edge caches still might route. Also lowering green instances might trigger more errors if in-flight. prefer weight rollback first.

ev an-sre: rolled weights back to blue 100% at 3701234720. confirm: green-serving-queries -> 0 on control plane.

deploy-bot: traffic shift event recorded: 3701234720 revert to blue (100%).

maya-eng: monitoring logs/latency. edge 502s drop to near baseline within ~40s for most nodes; some cache regions still show residual 502s for ~3m.

thomas-customer-success: support updated affected customers; currently 2 tenants saw degraded user flows for ~4 minutes. CS offered incident update and compensation offer where warranted.

lisa-reliability: running post-rollback checks: healthchecks ok, error budget unaffected past SLO after rollback. marking incident as mitigated; still keeping page in case of reappearance.

ev an-sre: creating follow-up action items: 1) audit edge cache TTL variance across providers, 2) add pre-flip probe that validates edge peel-over for <1% error before we increase weight, 3) document feature-flag fallback path in runbook.

ops-runbook-bot: action items recorded: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC12345/actions

maya-eng: notable root/lead hypothesis: partial routing due to edge cache route-staleness + release had a subtle startup behavior causing transient 5xx under spike. will schedule canary with connection-stabilization probe next time.

thomas-customer-success: customers notified, CS unhappy but acceptable given mitigation speed. closing customer impact window: 3701234680 - 3701234940 (approx).

ev an-sre: marking as resolved in PagerDuty and moving to postmortem. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

lisa-reliability: filing postmortem draft and tagging DRI (maya-eng, evan-sre). link: https://redwood.internal/pm/INC12345-draft

maya-eng: thanks all — will follow up with plan to tighten edge TTLs and add the pre-flip probe.
